correctness.rationale: Tree geodesics contain at most two pendant edges. At most two chosen spine edges are possible; with one, all chosen pendants must lie to one side; with two, all chosen pendants must lie strictly between. Every compatible set is a subset of exactly one or more of the displayed configurations. Positive leaf multiplicities exclude every omitted-edge extension at each listed facet. The facet bijection gives the polynomial and triangular count. The minimum uses the least prefix/suffix/interior sums; unlimited r gives an unbounded size spread. The independently constructed shortest-path tester exhaustively compared 135720 subsets from 60 small instances with both complete-set and facet collections.

value.rationale: Counting inclusion-maximal edge-general-position sets, rather than maximum-cardinality sets, is a natural and genuinely distinct question. This complete family classification with arbitrary positive leaf multiplicities yields the surprising exact invariance m(m+1)/2 in an unboundedly growing tree family, the full facet-size polynomial, and an exact lower invariant; the sizes vary by arbitrarily large amounts despite fixed facet count. These facts are not supplied by the known tree maximum or all-set cardinality polynomial, and the full nontrivial family is not an arbitrary small numerical slice.
